title: Single-solution wet mopping
audience: Cleaners in any cleaning-group business who wet mop hard floors using one diluted solution.
learningOutcomes: Prepare one diluted solution to the product label directions, water first, and mark the bucket.
Mop in manageable sections, edges first, working from the far point toward the door.
Remove overspill from skirting boards with a clean damp cloth before the floor is mopped.
Wring the mop without tipping the bucket, and keep the bucket behind you at all times.
Confirm the floor surface type before choosing a method, and leave the floor dry and free of slip risk before removing signs.

instruction.heading: Why one solution and one method
instruction.body: Single-solution mopping uses one diluted product in one bucket. That keeps the method simple and reduces the chance of mixing products. It is a wet method, so the risks are slips, over-wetting and damage to floors that cannot take water. Good mopping is planned before the bucket is filled: the surface type, the level of soil, the area to be done in one go, and how long the floor needs to dry.

instruction.heading: Preparing the solution
instruction.body: Fill the bucket with water first, then add the product at the dilution the label or the approved procedure gives. Do not add a second product, and do not pour product into a bucket of mop water without measuring it. Mark the bucket with the product and the time it was made, so the team knows what is in it. Check that the mop and cloths are washed and clean before you start. Confirm the floor surface type from the approved procedure before you choose the method, because not every floor takes a wet mop.

instruction.heading: Mopping technique
instruction.body: Work in a section you can reach comfortably, because over-stretching is a manual handling risk and produces uneven results. Keep the bucket behind you so you never step through the mop water. Start at the outside edges of the room and wipe overspill off the skirting boards with a clean damp cloth. Use a scouring pad only for stubborn marks, and only on a surface that is not polished, as the approved procedure directs. Then mop the middle of the room, working from the point furthest from the door toward the door, and rinse the mop often so that you are not spreading dirty water.

instruction.heading: Wringing, drying and finishing
instruction.body: Wring the mop out over the bucket, with the bucket held between your feet so that it cannot tip and pour water across the floor. Change the mop water when it looks dirty. Leave the area signposted until the floor is fully dry. Remove warning signs and close ventilation only once the floor is dry, because a damp floor is still a slip hazard. A floor that dries quickly means customers are less likely to slip.

instruction.heading: Storage after the job
instruction.body: Mop heads go head up to air-dry. Buckets are washed and stored upside down with cloths hung over the top. Keep the whole set in its colour group, so that the mop used on floors is never used on a washroom or kitchen surface.

procedure: Identify the floor surface type and confirm the approved method for it before you choose a product.
Put on gloves. Fill the bucket with water first, then add the measured product at the label dilution.
Mark the bucket with the product and time it was made, then position it so you can work without stepping into it.
Put up warning signs, and make trailing cables and open sockets safe.
Wipe the skirting boards and edges with a clean damp cloth, then mop the outside edges of the section.
Mop the middle of the section from the far point toward the door, rinsing the mop often.
Wring the mop over the bucket with the bucket between your feet. Change the water when it looks dirty.
Confirm the floor is dry and free of slip risk, then remove signs and close ventilation. Wash and store all equipment.

workedExamples.situation: A foyer has a polished timber floor and scuff marks by the doors. The bucket was filled with product before any water was added.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Which steps must be corrected before you mop?
workedExamples.reasoning: Empty the bucket and refill it with water first, then add the product at the label dilution. Check the approved method for polished timber before you mop, and confirm that a wet method is allowed. Do not use a scouring pad on a polished surface.

workedExamples.situation: A corridor is still wet from an earlier team's mop, and the client needs the space back in 30 minutes.
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not mop onto a floor that is not ready. Sign-post the area, let the floor dry as far as the procedure requires, and tell the supervisor that the timing is not realistic. Mopping over an unfinished, wet floor creates a slip risk and gives poor results.

equipmentAndPpe: Gloves, worn at all times when using chemicals.
Eye protection when the SDS requires it or when diluting a concentrate.
Colour-coded bucket, mop and cloths for the zone.
Clean scouring pad, used only where the approved procedure allows.
Mop wringer or bucket with wringing insert, where fitted.
Ventilation: open windows or doors where possible.

commonErrors.error: Pouring the product into the bucket first, which causes foam and splashback.
commonErrors.prevention: Water first, then the measured product at the label dilution.

commonErrors.error: Trying to mop a whole large room in one pass.
commonErrors.prevention: Divide the room into sections you can reach without stretching.

commonErrors.error: Leaving the bucket in front of you as you work.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep the bucket behind you at all times.

commonErrors.error: Removing the warning signs before the floor is dry.
commonErrors.prevention: Confirm the floor is dry before removing any sign.

commonErrors.error: Using a scouring pad on a polished floor.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the surface type and the approved method before any scouring.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: A wet floor is a slip hazard until it is dry.
Chemical use follows “Chemical competency: reading labels and safety data sheets”: check the label and SDS, dilute to the label, and never combine products.
Manual handling: keep sections manageable and avoid over-stretching.
Protect customer property: mopping must not damage other floor surfaces. Check the surface type before any wet cleaning.

qualityStandard: Solution prepared water first, to the label dilution, with the bucket marked.
Edges and skirting cleaned before the middle; the middle mopped from the far point toward the door.
Floor dry and free of visible streaks before warning signs are removed.
No trailing cable or open socket left in the work area.
documentationEvidence: Bucket marking record showing product, dilution and time.
Record of any floor surface damage or defect found before mopping.
Record of the time the floor was confirmed dry and signs were removed.
summary: One solution, water first, at the label dilution, and a marked bucket.
Mop in manageable sections: edges first, then the middle toward the door.
The bucket stays behind you, and the mop is wrung over it between your feet.
Signs stay up until the floor is dry.

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the correct order for making a single-solution mop bucket?
options: Product first, then the water and then stir the bucket well
Water first, then the measured product at the label dilution
Hot water only, with no product and no detergent at all

knowledgeChecks.question: In single-solution wet mopping, where should the bucket sit?
options: Behind you, so you do not step through the mop water
In front of you, so it is easy to reach as you move forward
Anywhere, provided the floor is dry and the mop is wet

knowledgeChecks.question: When can the warning signs be removed after a wet mop?
options: As soon as the mopping is finished and the floor looks clean
When the floor is fully dry and the slip risk has passed
When the client asks you to move on and the client is happy
